label: prf:qou-obstruction-reduction
title: Proof of qou obstruction reduction
html:
Proof. Proof of qou obstruction reduction

What the axioms supply, and what they do not. Three facts are relevant to the hypothesis of the Wigner axiom.

Step 1: Observability kills HH^0. The QOU axiom \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 (observability) is the statement

HH^0(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) = \mathrm{Ad}^G = 0.

The adjoint representation of a semisimple group has no invariant vectors (equivalently: \mathfrak{g} has trivial centre).

Step 2: Duality is cohomology-to-homology, with a twist. For a Noetherian Hopf algebra H that is Artin--Schelter Gorenstein of dimension d — this covers \mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}), \mathcal{O}(G), \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}) and \mathcal{O}_q(G) — Brown and Zhang [brown-zhang-2008] prove the twisted Poincaré duality

HH^{i}(H, M) \;\cong\; HH_{d-i}(H, {}_{\nu}M),

where \nu is the Nakayama automorphism of H: trivial up to an inner automorphism for \mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}) and \mathcal{O}(G), and non-trivial for the quantum groups. The untwisted form fails at q \neq 1: the Hochschild homology of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2) drops in top degree [feng-tsygan-1991], and the one-dimensional top group reappears only in the twisted theory [hadfield-krahmer-2005]. With d = \dim G = 3 the relevant identification is HH^2(H, \mathrm{Ad}) \cong HH_1(H, {}_{\nu}\mathrm{Ad}) — first Hochschild homology with twisted coefficients, not the dual of HH^1.

Step 3: At the classical point the space is zero. For H = \mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}) one has HH^n(\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}), M) \cong H^n(\mathfrak{g}, M) with M carrying the adjoint action, and Whitehead's lemmas [weibel1994] give H^1(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^2(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0 for \mathfrak{g} semisimple in characteristic 0 and M finite-dimensional, hence for the locally finite \mathrm{Ad}(A). So \mathrm{Obs} = 0 at q = 1. The one-dimensionality of the obstruction space at q \neq 1 is therefore not a consequence of the axioms; it is the first clause of the Wigner axiom, and the identification of its generator with the Euler class is the second.

Proof of (a). By the second clause the generator w(A) maps to e(\xi) = e(TM_0) \in H^2(M_0; \mathbb{Z}). The Euler class of the tangent bundle of a closed oriented surface integrates to its Euler characteristic (Poincaré–Hopf), so \langle e(TM_0), [M_0] \rangle = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0). Since the obstruction space is one-dimensional by the first clause, the class is determined by this integer. No Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg identification is used. \square

Proof of (b). This is the Kummer specialisation (Kummer): \kappa_0 \bmod n = 0 in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) / nH^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) iff n divides \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0). Equivalently, the motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A is non-trivial at every finite place p \nmid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) (motivic perpetual obstruction, proved via Route A: prime-ideal collapse, C = a_0(-1) + 2 \cdot a_1(-1)). \square
